correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the stationary telegraph trajectory makes X_t a centered Gaussian with random variance 2(mu t+a integral S), yielding kappa_{2m}(X_t)=(2m)!/m! kappa_m(A_t) and odd integrated-spin cumulants zero. Integrated pair correlation e^{-2k|s-u|} yields kappa4=24a^2 f(x)/(2k)^2. The time-ordered connected 4-spin correlation is -2 exp[-2k(gap1+2gap2+gap3)], so kappa8=-80640a^4 I(x)/(2k)^4; coefficient normalization checked independently using a 2x2 tilted generator. Differentiation gives P(x)=2e^{2x}(I'f-2If')=(4-x)e^{2x}-(2x^2+8)e^x+(x+4); its first six series coefficients vanish and for all n>=6 the coefficient [2^{n-1}(8-n)-2n(n-1)-8]/n!<0 (verify n=6,7 then n>=8). Thus Q decreases strictly, with endpoints from f~x^2/2, I~x^4/24 and large x. Algebraic inverse x, k=x/(2t), mu=V/(2t), a=x sqrt(C/(24f))/t proves necessity/sufficiency including strict a<mu. Independent symbolic Laplace identity and three tilted-generator checks passed. Population cumulants only; no statistical estimation claim.

value.rationale: Provides a complete, sharp population identifiability and feasibility test for a natural stochastic-diffusivity model using measurements at one fixed time, resolving intrinsic parameter ambiguity without multi-time trajectories. The positivity inequality and sharp ratio image matter physically. It is a mathematically motivated inverse theorem, not merely recomputation of known forward cumulants.

final_claim: For a stationary symmetric 2-state diffusivity with D_+=mu+a, D_-=mu-a strictly positive, switch rate k>0, known t>0, the population cumulants (kappa_2,kappa_4,kappa_8) uniquely determine (mu,a,k) up to state-label swap. With x=2kt, f=x-1+e^-x, I=x/2-5/4+(x+1)e^-x+e^-2x/4, Q=-kappa_8/kappa_4^2=140I/f^2 decreases bijectively from 70/3 to 0; the sharp realization inequality is C<6V^2 f(x)/x^2.
limitations: Unindexed inverse stochastic-process literature could contain an equivalent exact single-time cumulant identifiability result.
